subject: Animation
title: Frame Rates: 12, 24, or 60?
description: Learn Frame Rates: 12, 24, or 60? in one minute.

hook.text: Most animation runs at 24 frames per second, but animators often draw only 12 unique images per second.

buildup.text: Animating on twos means each drawing is held for two frames. On ones means a new drawing every frame.

discovery.text: Anime often uses 8 to 12 unique drawings per second, creating its distinctive snappier visual rhythm.

twist.text: Higher frame rates do not always look better. The Hobbit at 48fps was criticized for looking too real and cheap.

climax.text: Frame rate is not about more or less — it is about choosing the right rhythm for the story's feel.

punchline.text: More frames per second does not always mean better animation.

quiz.question: What does 'animating on twos' mean?
options: Using two animators for the same scene
Each unique drawing is held for two frames, resulting in 12 drawings per second at 24fps
Drawing two versions of every character

details.summary: Frame rate determines how many individual images appear per second: 12 fps gives a classic 'animated' look, 24 fps is standard film, and 60 fps produces ultra-smooth motion. Animators choose rates to match their artistic intent.
details.whyItMatters: Frame rate is not just a technical choice — it fundamentally changes how animation feels. Higher rates look smoother but can feel uncanny; lower rates feel more handcrafted and traditionally animated.
takeaways: 12 fps gives a classic hand-drawn animation feel
24 fps is the standard for feature animation and cinema
Higher frame rates feel smoother but can lose traditional charm

faq.question: Why do many animated films use 12 frames per second?
faq.answer: Animating 'on twos' (12 unique drawings per second shown at 24 fps) halves the work while creating a pleasing, slightly stylized look. Full 24 fps animation is reserved for fast actions or scenes requiring smoothness.

faq.question: Is higher frame rate always better for animation?
faq.answer: No. The Hobbit at 48 fps was criticized for looking too real and losing cinematic quality. Into the Spider-Verse deliberately used low frame rates for style. Frame rate is an artistic choice, not a quality scale.
